items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Quite a lot of the songs found their way over there and were sung, very well sometimes, by Jean Sablon — and in England too, absolutely.

ctx.x: Did the American songwriters of the 30s and 40s, did their songs make it over to England?

Yeah, quite a few of them did. I mean a lot of them made it further than anywhere else on the continent. I mean in France you get songs like “Ces Petit Choses” which is “These Foolish Things,” you know, and I mean they sang them with French lyrics. Quite a lot of the songs found their way over there and were sung, very well sometimes, by Jean Sablon — and in England too, absolutely. I mean very often the British bands would record a cover version of an American hit and things like that. Sure. And then of course…
So was your jazz learning mostly from records?
